title: UN Chief Urges Global AI Safety Framework as Tech Power Concentrates
title_zh: 联合国秘书长呼吁建立全球人工智能安全框架，警惕科技权力高度集中
source_name: UN News — “UN chief urges talks on global AI safety framework, warns of historic shift in power”
summary_zh: 2026年11月23日，联合国与巴巴多斯共同主办布里奇敦人工智能安全特别峰会。联合国秘书长古特雷斯呼吁各国启动谈判，建立具有包容性的多边人工智能风险管理框架，并警告人工智能正在引发人类历史上最大规模的权力转移——权力正从国家与公共机构流向少数科技企业。与会领导人还讨论了问责机制、应急干预权限、发展中国家技术能力建设以及多语种安全测试等议题，强调应通过透明规则与独立监督确保人工智能造福全人类。
paragraphs: On 23 November 2026, the United Nations and Barbados co-hosted the Bridgetown Special Summit on AI Safety in the Caribbean island's capital. At the close of the meeting, UN Secretary-General António Guterres urged member states to begin talks on a global framework for managing the risks of artificial intelligence. He warned that existing protections remain fragmented and that governments are too often playing catch-up as powerful new tools advance.

Speaking alongside Barbadian Prime Minister Mia Mottley, Guterres described the rapid rise of AI as the biggest transfer of power in human history. Unlike earlier shifts between nations, influence is now moving away from states and public institutions toward a small number of private technology companies. He also noted that recent system outages and cyberattacks show how vulnerable modern infrastructure has become, especially when advanced models act in ways that even their developers do not always anticipate.

Leaders at the summit stressed that both major economies and smaller countries need a voice in shaping AI rules. Mottley pointed out that small states are frequently excluded from decisions that directly affect their citizens. She argued that governments must be able to demand accountability from AI companies when harm occurs and retain an emergency kill switch to shut down dangerous systems. In a video message, French President Emmanuel Macron added that agreeing to shared security principles should be a condition for market access.

Another key concern in Bridgetown was the unequal capacity of countries to test and regulate emerging technology. Because AI risks cross national borders, Guterres warned that uneven protection could deepen global inequality and called for a new fund to support developing nations. A report released by a UN-backed scientific panel also showed why local testing is essential: many AI models perform far worse and become less reliable in African languages and Caribbean creoles than in widely spoken languages.

Summit participants emphasized that stronger rules are not intended to block technological progress or spread fear. Artificial intelligence already offers clear benefits, from strengthening healthcare systems to speeding up scientific research. However, Guterres concluded that the growth of AI models cannot move faster than society's ability to keep them safe. Building shared testing methods, clear transparency standards and independent oversight will help ensure that AI serves all humanity.
paragraphs_zh: 2026年11月23日，联合国与巴巴多斯在这个加勒比岛国首都联合主办了布里奇敦人工智能安全特别峰会。在会议闭幕时，联合国秘书长古特雷斯敦促各成员国就建立管理人工智能风险的全球框架启动谈判。他警告称，现有的防护措施仍然碎片化，随着强大的新工具不断发展，各国政府往往只能疲于追赶。
古特雷斯在与巴巴多斯总理米娅·莫特利共同出席活动时，将人工智能的迅速崛起形容为人类历史上最大规模的权力转移。与以往国家之间的权力更迭不同，如今的影响力正从国家和公共机构流向少数私营科技公司。他还指出，近期的系统中断和网络攻击表明现代基础设施已变得十分脆弱，尤其是当先进模型以连开发者都未必总能预料的方式运作时。
出席峰会的领导人强调，主要经济体和较小国家都应当在制定人工智能规则方面拥有发言权。莫特利指出，小国经常被排除在直接影响本国公民的决策之外。她认为，当人工智能造成损害时，政府必须能够向相关企业追究责任，并保留在紧急情况下关闭危险系统的“终止开关”。法国总统马克龙在视频致辞中也补充道，认同共同的安全原则应成为进入市场的前提条件。
布里奇敦峰会的另一项核心关切是各国在测试和监管新兴技术方面的能力不均。由于人工智能风险跨越国界，古特雷斯警告称，防护水平的不平衡可能会加剧全球不平等，并呼吁设立一项新基金来支持发展中国家。联合国支持的科学小组发布的一份报告也说明了开展本地测试的重要性：在非洲语言和加勒比克里奥尔语中，许多人工智能模型的表现远逊于通用语言，可靠性也更低。
与会各方强调，制定更有力的规则并非为了阻碍技术进步或制造恐慌。人工智能已经展现出实实在在的益处，从增强医疗系统到加快科学研究莫不如此。然而，古特雷斯总结道，人工智能模型的发展速度不能超过人类社会保障其安全的能力。建立共享的测试方法、明确的透明度标准以及独立的监督机制，将有助于确保人工智能造福全人类。

questions.prompt: What is the main focus of the passage?
options: Barbados's plan to replace all traditional government offices with artificial intelligence tools.
A UN-backed summit calling for a global AI safety framework to address shifting power, accountability and unequal capacity.
Why French technology companies have decided to stop developing advanced AI models.
How recent cyberattacks completely destroyed the global internet infrastructure in 2026.
questions.explanation: 全文围绕联合国与巴巴多斯共同主办的布里奇敦人工智能安全特别峰会展开，介绍了各国就建立全球人工智能风险管理框架、应对科技权力集中、追究企业责任以及缩小各国安全监管能力差距所展开的讨论。其他选项均与原文不符或属无中生有。

evidence.quote: At the close of the meeting, UN Secretary-General António Guterres urged member states to begin talks on a global framework for managing the risks of artificial intelligence.

questions.prompt: According to the fourth paragraph, what did a UN-backed scientific panel find about many AI models?
options: They are already equally reliable in every African and Caribbean language.
They perform much worse and are less reliable in African languages and Caribbean creoles.
They can only operate inside countries that contribute to the new UN fund.
They no longer require local testing once global standards are approved.
questions.explanation: 第四段明确指出，由联合国支持的科学小组发布的报告显示，与通用语言相比，许多人工智能模型在非洲语言和加勒比克里奥尔语中的表现要差得多，可靠性也更低。因此本地测试十分必要。

evidence.quote: many AI models perform far worse and become less reliable in African languages and Caribbean creoles than in widely spoken languages.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from the final paragraph about the goal of stronger AI regulation?
options: It aims to halt all scientific and healthcare uses of artificial intelligence.
It is meant to keep AI safety controls aligned with the speed of technological development.
It will allow technology companies to operate without any independent oversight.
It assumes that AI models are already completely safe without transparency standards.
questions.explanation: 最后一段指出，加强规则并非为了阻碍技术进步，而是强调模型的发展不能快于社会保障其安全的能力，需要通过共享测试方法、透明度和独立监督来实现安全可控，由此可推断监管的目标是让安全控制跟上技术发展的步伐。其余三项均与文意相反。

evidence.quote: However, Guterres concluded that the growth of AI models cannot move faster than society's ability to keep them safe.
